# Representation Clause

Prepares an embedded Operation Mandate named `Operation delegation` for a fixed delegate, target and set of operations. The `grant` action creates the mandate; the owner must separately approve its exact pending document before it provides usable authority.

The clause uses these configuration values:

- `parameters.owner`: the owner’s channel name. It must match `call/channel`. The channel at `/contracts/<owner>` becomes the mandate’s `contracts.authorityHolderChannel` and supplies the target channel name for every grant.
- `parameters.delegate`: the representative’s channel name. `/contracts/<delegate>` must exist; its channel becomes `contracts.authorizedActorChannel`.
- `parameters.target`: the target document’s path in the document where the clause executes. Each grant’s `target.initialDocument` references the exact Blue identity of the value at `<target>/contracts/initialized/document`, fixing the target lineage when `grant` runs.
- `parameters.operations`: operation names used as both scope keys and each grant’s `target.operation`. Operation names must be nonempty. Repeated names occupy the same scope entry; an empty collection supplies no operation authority.
- `bindings.mandate`: a non-root document pointer, defaulting to `/mandate`. It selects both the destination for the created mandate and its embedded processing location.

No defaults are declared for `owner`, `delegate`, `target` or `operations`. Delegation is determined by these clause parameters, rather than caller-selected request fields.

`grant` first rejects a different calling channel with `MANDATE_OWNER_REQUIRED`, then rejects an undeclared delegate with `DECLARED_REPRESENTATIVE_REQUIRED`. These checks also precede duplicate handling. If any value already exists at `bindings.mandate`, the action sets `actionResult.outcome` to `duplicate` without checking that value’s identity, contents or lifecycle status, and without replacing it. Otherwise, it adds the constructed mandate and sets `actionResult` to `{outcome: "acceptedNew", path: <destination>}`. Neither outcome establishes approval or completion of a delegated target operation.

Named connections under `bindings.grant` determine invocation; this type supplies no automatic trigger. A `workflow` connection uses `party` when supplied, otherwise `channel`, as its authenticated channel. Connection `when` defaults to true and skips execution when false. `parameters.conditions.grant` defaults to true and rejects execution when false. Optional `before` steps run before the grant body and its guards. Only `acceptedNew` proceeds to `after` steps and can mark a `once` connection fired; subsequent triggers of that fired connection are skipped. `once` defaults to false. Changes to an installed clause’s configuration require a new clause key.

The created mandate has its own document root: `/status`, `/scope`, `/approvedAt` and `/terminatedAt` belong to that embedded document. Genuine initialization establishes `Pending`, removes supplied approval and termination timestamps, and emits `Mandate Initialized`. Pending has no usable authority. Missing lifecycle values do not establish a status.

The owner’s direct `approveMandate` operation accepts an empty request, requires `Pending` and `requireExactDocumentVersion: true` for the exact reviewed pending document, and approves the whole program. Successful approval changes status to `Active`, records `approvedAt` and emits `Mandate Approved`. No delegate countersignature is required. The holder’s `terminateMandate` accepts only a nonempty `reason` while Pending or Active. Its internal `Mandate Termination Requested` signal causes scope clearing, a `Scope Changed` event, permanent `Terminated` status, `terminatedAt`, a `Mandate Terminated` event and termination of mandate processing. Both timestamps use causal event time in microseconds. Termination does not reverse completed target actions.

The generated scope adds no document or request predicates and no use counter. Grants can support repeated calls while eligible. Actual delegation requires supported Mandates processing, distinct authenticated holder and delegate actors, admitted delegate participation in the target, verified approval and complete relevant prior history, and a matching active grant. Missing required history means waiting. Target operation guards still apply, and an authorized attempt does not guarantee success. Scope content, copied events or a mandate reference alone do not prove authority.
